open_points.subject: expense correction request contract
open_points.text: “A correction body with a missing or wrongly typed field … is refused” does not identify which correction fields are required; M28 permits corrections of supplier, date, amount and included, while only an amount correction is said to require a matching allocation adjustment.
open_points.question: Is correction a full replacement requiring total and a complete non-empty allocation set on every call, or may a caller correct supplier, date or inclusion without supplying replacement allocations?
options: Every correction requires all correction fields and a complete replacement allocation set.
Only an amount correction requires total and replacement allocations; other fields may be corrected independently.
The request is a patch, with requirements derived from the fields present.
open_points.default_guess: Require a full correction body and a complete replacement allocation set.

witness.initial: Expense E belongs to project P, totals EUR 100, and has one valid EUR 100 allocation.
events: An authorized operator submits a correction changing only E’s supplier and omits total and allocations.
outcomes: Request decoding refuses the correction with HTTP 422 because total and allocations are required.
The supplier is corrected successfully while the existing total and allocations remain unchanged.
witness.observer: The operator calling the correction route

open_points.subject: expense correction refusal representation
open_points.text: Expense creation refusals are explicitly “HTTP 422 with an empty body”, but the added correction rule says only “a refused total or allocation answers 422” and “an expense of no or another project 409”.
open_points.question: What response body, if any, accompanies correction refusals with status 422 or 409?
options: They carry a generic fixed error body.
They carry validation or conflict details identifying the failed check.
open_points.default_guess: Use empty bodies, matching the stated expense-creation error policy and minimizing disclosure.

witness.initial: An authorized operator has access to project P and submits a correction whose allocation sum differs from the proposed total.
events: The correction reaches allocation validation and is refused.
outcomes: The operator receives HTTP 422 with an empty body.
The operator receives HTTP 422 with a body describing the allocation-sum failure.
witness.observer: The operator and any API client handling the error

open_points.subject: A31 authorization review versus pre-guard correction decoding
open_points.text: A31 says authorization affects “every project-scoped operation” through A4, whose first check is the valid session, while changed A7 says a malformed correction body “is refused by request decoding before the guard.”
open_points.question: Is request decoding formally outside A4’s “every project-scoped operation” sequence, making malformed correction bodies an intentional pre-authentication refusal, or must the session failure win?
options: Decode the correction first and return HTTP 422 without authenticating.
Run authentication before body decoding so the concealed authentication rejection wins.
Decode only enough to route the request, authenticate, then perform detailed correction decoding.
open_points.default_guess: Treat transport decoding as outside the project operation and return HTTP 422 before the guard, as A7 states explicitly.

witness.initial: A request has an invalid or absent staff session and a correction body with a missing required field.
events: The caller sends the request to a project-scoped expense-correction route.
outcomes: Changed A7 is applied literally: decoding stops the request with HTTP 422 before authentication.
A4/A31 is applied literally to every project operation: the invalid session produces the concealed authentication rejection before correction validation.
